data.description: Add workspace/organization identifiers to RiotPlans so VS Code can scope plan discovery and tree filtering per workspace, mirroring Protokoll project binding behavior.

data.note: Terminology decision needed: prefer 'workspace' for VS Code alignment, but support 'organization' as a user-facing alias if needed. Primary requirement is deterministic scoping/filtering of plans by an identifier bound to the current VS Code workspace.

data.constraint: Plan listing/query APIs must support filtering by workspace identifier without breaking existing clients that do not send the filter.
The workspace identifier must be persisted per VS Code workspace (workspaceState), not globally, so each workspace remembers its own scope.

data.question: Should a single plan be allowed in multiple workspaces (array of ids) or exactly one workspace id?

data.description: Protokoll stores transcript filter preferences in VS Code workspaceState, including project filter key protokoll.projectFilter. This validates workspace-scoped persisted filtering UX for RiotPlan workspace identifiers.
data.summary: Protokoll uses workspaceState for project filters and sort/status settings.

data.name: Hybrid Context Identifier
data.description: Introduce contextId as neutral canonical key with type metadata (workspace|organization). VS Code defaults to workspace type and can later support organization contexts.
tradeoffs: Pros: Extensible for future grouping modes
Cons: More abstraction and complexity up front
Cons: Potentially slower to deliver immediate user value
assumptions: Future roadmap may require more than one grouping primitive

data.name: Workspace-First Identifier
data.description: Use workspaceId as canonical plan metadata field and query filter. Persist selected workspaceId in VS Code workspaceState. Keep optional display alias 'Organization' in UI copy where helpful.
tradeoffs: Pros: Aligns with VS Code terminology and workspace-scoped settings APIs
Pros: Clear mapping from open workspace to plan filter context
Cons: Some users may conceptually think in organizations, not workspaces
assumptions: Most users have one dominant organization per workspace
Workspace folder context is stable enough for persisted bindings

data.name: Organization-First Identifier
data.description: Use organizationId as canonical metadata and filter key, with optional workspace mapping layer in VS Code that binds each workspace to an organizationId.
tradeoffs: Pros: Better future multi-workspace organization aggregation
Cons: Adds mapping indirection for basic VS Code workflows
Cons: More migration and config surface
assumptions: Users often want to view multiple repositories under one organization identity

data.reason: This best matches VS Code workspace semantics and Protokoll’s existing workspaceState-based filtering UX while still allowing organization terminology as a user-facing alias.
